intro_html: Chapli kebabs come from Peshawar and they are nothing like the smooth ground meat kebabs you get at most Pakistani restaurants. These are wide, flat, craggy patties packed with tomato, onion, cilantro, and whole coriander seeds that you crush yourself so they crunch. Pomegranate molasses brings the sour note that makes them unmistakable. Traditionally they are shallow fried one at a time, which is a nightmare at this scale, so we bake them on sheet pans instead and get the same crisp edges with none of the standing around.
cost_closing_html: About $1.56 a bowl for Peshawari kebabs that most people only ever eat at a restaurant.
shop_smart: Crush whole coriander seeds yourself. The whole seed is cheaper than the ground jar and the crunch of the cracked seed is the entire texture of a chapli kebab.
Tomato and onion in the mix stretch the beef. That is traditional, not a shortcut, and it is why the meat number stays modest while the patties stay big.
Pomegranate molasses is one bottle you will keep reaching for. It lasts a long time in the fridge and there is no clean substitute for what it does here.
Bake, do not fry. Frying fourteen servings of patties eats a bottle of oil and an hour of your evening. Sheet pans in a hot oven get you there while you cook the rice.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Crush the whole coriander seeds coarsely, then mix them with the ground cumin, red pepper flakes, chili powder, black pepper, and salt.
Combine the ground beef with the finely chopped red onion, green onions, minced jalapeno, garlic, ginger, cilantro, eggs, all-purpose flour, pomegranate molasses, and the spice mix.
Fold in the drained diced tomatoes last and gently, so they stay in pieces instead of turning the mixture to slurry.
Chill the mixture for thirty minutes, which makes it far easier to shape.
Form wide, flat, thin patties, brush the sheet pans and the tops with the vegetable oil, and lay them out without touching.
Bake at 425 degrees, flipping once, until browned and crisp at the edges and cooked through.
Cook the rice according to the package while the kebabs bake.
portion_html: Weigh the rice pot, subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and divide by 14 for an even base in every container. Then split the kebabs evenly across the fourteen. Every bowl lands near 607 calories with 26 grams of protein. Reheat them in a hot oven or a dry pan rather than the microwave if you want to keep the crisp edges.

head.keywords: chapli kebab, pakistani kebab, peshawari kabab, sheet pan kebabs, pakistani meal prep, budget beef kebabs
steps: Coarsely crush the whole coriander seeds and mix with the other spices.
Combine the beef with onion, herbs, egg, flour, pomegranate molasses, and spices.
Fold in drained diced tomatoes gently and chill the mixture.
Shape wide flat patties and lay them on oiled sheet pans.
Bake at 425F, flipping once, until crisp and cooked through.
Cook the rice and portion kebabs over it into 14 containers.
